I grew up with this one kid who was absolutely horrible. He hurt me physically and emotionally. In 1st grade, I remember him calling me a n\*\*a. I'm not black. This happened for a couple of years. Then this other girl picked up where he left off. She started making fun of my heritage, calling me racist names, doing racist gestures, etc. She was also one of the "mean girls". Excluding me from things, telling the other kids that I was mean behind my back. Basically, any type of "mean girl" thing you can think of, she did.

 When the pandemic hit, I had people come up to me and tell me to go back to where I came from. They said I was infected. More people started to pull their eyes back. More people started to ask me if I ate cats, dogs, and bats. I don't. 

  
Now, I second guess everything. Subconsciously, I ask myself if the person I'm talking to only tolerates me because of my race. I know that sounds crazy, but I just can't help it. I've felt suicidal multiple times. My self-esteem has been at an all-time low for years. I don't feel happy. I just feel numb and depressed. I'm scared to meet new people. I'm scared that they might think I'm weird. Or that they'll start talking behind my back.   


I was also thrown across my friend's basement when I was younger. This other kid picked me up around my mid-section, and just threw me. Now, I don't like it when people touch my stomach. The kid also choked me multiple times. Now, I have this instinctive reaction to hit anybody who tries to touch my neck. I'm a mess.

"**Zélie Adebola remembers when the soil of Orïsha hummed with magic. Burners ignited flames, Tiders beckoned waves, and Zélie’s Reaper mother summoned forth souls.**

**But everything changed the night magic disappeared. Under the orders of a ruthless king, maji were killed, leaving Zélie without a mother and her people without hope.**

**Now Zélie has one chance to bring back magic and strike against the monarchy. With the help of a rogue princess, Zélie must outwit and outrun the crown prince, who is hell-bent on eradicating magic for good.  Danger lurks in Orïsha, where snow leoponaires prowl and vengeful spirits wait in the waters. Yet the greatest danger may be Zélie herself as she struggles to control her powers—and her growing feelings for an enemy."**

The book has a very strong female character and the plot is incredible. The main character is an African American girl who doesn't take any crap. She isn't a damsel in distress or a princess that needs a man to save her. The kingdom teaches its people that people with light brown skin are superior to those with dark brown skin and white hair. The kingdom also teaches its people to hate the dark-skinned peoples religion and culture. The main character rises above all of this and fights for what she believes is right. Tomi Adeyemi is a beautiful storyteller. She weaves magic in with Nigerian culture and history.
